bet.dominantBottleneck: Time-sensitive repetitive search/counting workload exceeding human and electromechanical clerical capacity, where the binding constraint is the speed of repeated candidate testing against logical/statistical constraints given that human analysts must still set hypotheses and interpret outputs.

routes.route: scale human clerical analysis and add more operators
routes.reason: Human headcount cannot keep pace with time-sensitive search workloads; adding operators expanely amplifies labor cost, introduces propagation of errors and does not address switching speed. It remains a complement for hypothesis choice and interpretation but is not the primary accelerator.

routes.route: build more electromechanical special-purpose search machines using known cipher structure
routes.reason: Electromechanical relays exploit known structure and are proven, but mechanical switching speed is the limiting factor cited. Building more of them scales throughput only linearly and leaves the core latency bottleneck untouched, though they remain a viable fallback.

routes.route: build a special-purpose electronic statistical/counting machine fed by high-speed tape while humans set tests
routes.reason: Vacuum-tube switching/counting offers the step-change in speed needed, high-speed paper-tape/photoelectric input is technically plausible for streaming symbols, and the design stays within proven special-purpose scope (statistical/counting tests) without demanding all-purpose autonomy. Humans supply hypotheses, prepare data and interpret, which matches the evidenced human role. This is the smallest-scope route that directly attacks the switching-speed bottleneck before operational deadlines.

routes.route: attempt an all-purpose autonomous machine that discovers cipher structure without human hypotheses
routes.reason: It demands generality and machine discovery of cipher structure, requiring reconfiguration and program sophistication far beyond the available state of the art (no mature stored-program computers, no modern programming). It also violates the evidenced requirement that humans choose hypotheses/cribs. High risk of never arriving within operational deadlines.

routes.route: develop a large electronic numerical calculator for table production as a separate workload
routes.reason: Numerical table production is a real workload, but it is a separate problem and the evidence keeps rapid cipher search time-sensitive and primary. Spending scarce electronic effort and maintenance budget on a separate calculator could divert resources; pursue only after/if resources allow, not as the current decisive bet.

routes.route: treat human analysis, machine search and operational interpretation as one coupled workflow and optimize the current bottleneck rather than demanding generality
routes.reason: This is the right framing principle: it keeps the coupled workflow in view (humans set tests, machine searches, humans interpret) and targets the current bottleneck instead of demanding all-purpose generality. It should govern how the electronic machine is built and deployed, and it is consistent with the top route.
